content.overview: Section 47(1) provides that, subject to the provisions of section 43, sub-section (2) of section 50 and sub-section (1) of section 188—(a) every member of a company limited by shares and holding equity share capital therein shall have a right to vote on every resolution placed before the company; and (b) his voting right on a poll shall be in proportion to his share in the paid-up equity share capital of the company. Section 47(2) provides that every member holding any preference share capital shall, in respect of such capital, have a right to vote only on resolutions which directly affect the rights attached to his preference shares and any resolution for the winding up of the company or for the repayment or reduction of its equity or preference share capital, and his voting right on a poll shall be in proportion to his share in the paid-up preference share capital. Provided that the proportion of the voting rights of equity shareholders to the voting rights of the preference shareholders shall be in the same proportion as the paid-up capital in respect of the equity shares bears to the paid-up capital in respect of the preference shares. Provided further that where the dividend in respect of a class of preference shares has not been paid for a period of two years or more, such class of preference shareholders shall have a right to vote on all the resolutions placed before the company.
content.glance: Equity: vote on every resolution; poll proportional to paid-up equity. Preference: vote only on rights-affecting, winding-up or capital repayment/reduction resolutions; poll proportional to paid-up preference; equity:preference voting ratio tracks paid-up capital ratio; if preference dividend unpaid for 2 years or more, vote on all resolutions.
content.study: Subject to s. 43, s. 50(2) and s. 188(1), every equity member has a right to vote on every resolution; on a poll, voting right is proportional to paid-up equity share capital (s. 47(1)). Preference members vote only on resolutions that directly affect preference rights and on winding-up or repayment/reduction of equity or preference capital; on a poll, proportional to paid-up preference capital. The proportion of equity voting rights to preference voting rights is the same as the proportion of paid-up equity capital to paid-up preference capital. Where dividend on a class of preference shares has not been paid for two years or more, that class may vote on all resolutions (s. 47(2)). Current-law framing: identify class; apply equity or limited preference rule; check two-year dividend arrears for expanded preference voting.

sections.heading: Equity voting (s. 47(1))
sections.body: Subject to s. 43, s. 50(2) and s. 188(1): every equity member votes on every resolution; on a poll, votes proportional to paid-up equity share capital.

sections.heading: Preference voting — limited (s. 47(2))
sections.body: Preference members vote only on resolutions that directly affect preference rights and on winding-up or repayment/reduction of equity or preference capital; on a poll, proportional to paid-up preference capital. Equity:preference voting proportion tracks paid-up capital proportion.

sections.heading: Preference voting — expanded on arrears
sections.body: Where dividend on a class of preference shares has not been paid for a period of two years or more, that class shall have a right to vote on all resolutions placed before the company.

examples.title: Equity poll
examples.body: On a poll, an equity holder with twice the paid-up equity capital of another has twice the voting power under s. 47(1).

examples.title: Preference arrears
examples.body: Preference dividend unpaid for two years or more. That class may vote on all resolutions under the second proviso to s. 47(2).

hypotheticals.question: Can preference shareholders vote on ordinary business when dividends are current?
hypotheticals.analysis: Generally no, unless the resolution directly affects preference rights or is for winding-up or capital repayment/reduction. Two years’ arrears expands voting to all resolutions.

distinctions.title: Voting rights (s. 47) vs kinds of share capital (s. 43)
distinctions.left: Who may vote and on what

misconceptions.trap: Preference shareholders always vote on every resolution.
misconceptions.correction: Preference voting is generally limited to rights-affecting, winding-up and capital repayment/reduction resolutions, unless dividend is unpaid for two years or more.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 47 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify class of shares. II. Apply equity or preference voting rules. III. Check two-year dividend arrears. IV. Conclude on voting rights.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Share class; resolution type; arrears status; voting entitlement; precise relief.
